newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas ends higher after late rally.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas ends higher after late rally.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natural gas futures staged a late rally and settled higher Tuesday in moderate trade, with technical buying and firmer physical prices driving the complex through key resistance.
May jumped five cents to close at $2.114 per million British thermal units. June settled 3.3 cents higher at $2.164. Other deferreds ended up by 0.3 to 3.2 cents.

"We had a triple bottom at $2.035 (in May) and they couldn't break it down this morning. Short covering in the physical market just wouldn't allow the board to go lower," said a Midwest trader, referring to recent gains in the cash.
Most agreed cool Midwest and Eastern temperatures this month caught some short physical gas and helped drive cash prices 20-30 cents above index.
Technical traders said the "squeeze" in cash caught paper shorts by surprise, forcing some to cover as key resistance point were breached late last week and this week.
And while the technical picture has improved with the recent rally, some questioned how long current levels can be sustained, with milder spring weather likely to arrive soon.

Chart traders said May's close above key resistance at $2.095 left $2.16 as the next target. Further selling was likely at $2.21. May support was at $2.035, with further buying expected at $1.925, $1.88, $1.85 and $1.825.
In June, today's close above $2.145 should lead to a test of the $2.21-2.23 gap from mid-January. June support was pegged at $2.085 and then along the short-term up trendline in the $1.98 area.
Early estimates for Wednesday's weekly American Gas Association storage report ranged from a draw of 32 bcf to a build of 30 bcf versus a gain last year of 27 bcf.

In the cash, Gulf Coast prices were steady to up slightly Tuesday in the $2.04-2.09 area. Midcontinent pipes gained a similar amount to the mid-$1.90s. Gas at the New York city gate was quoted in the mid-$2.30s, little changed on the day.
The NYMEX 12-month Henry Hub strip rose 1.9 cents to $2.247. NYMEX said 40,926 Hub contracts traded, up from Monday's revised tally of 34,046.
NYMEX May natgas expires Thursday, April 24.

On the KCBT, May finished nine cents higher at $2.02, while deferreds ended mixed. The East/West spread narrowed by four cents to 9.4 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 782 lots changed hands, up sharply from Monday's total of 55.
KCBT May natgas expires Friday, April 25.
